ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The prepared oleic acid alcohol solution contains 0.6 mL of oleic acid per 1000 mL of the solution. Using a dropper, 50 drops of the above solution are added to a measuring cylinder, increasing the volume of the solution in the cylinder by 1 mL. When a drop of this solution is dripped into a shallow dish filled with water, the alcohol dissolves in the water, and the oleic acid spreads on the water surface, forming a stable monomolecular oil film as shown in the figure.

1. If the side length of each small square is $30\mathrm{mm}$, what is the area of the oleic acid film in square meters?
2. What is the volume of pure oleic acid in each drop of oleic acid alcohol solution in cubic meters?
3. Based on the above data, what is the estimated diameter of the oleic acid molecule in meters?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, it is an irregular oleic acid film boundary drawn on uniform graph paper. Estimating according to the squares covered by the boundary in the figure, counting the small squares that are close to complete as 1, and combining and converting the incomplete small squares at the edge, the oil film occupies about 85 small squares. Then reason and calculate: The side length of each small square is 30 mm = 0.03 m, so the area of each small square is (0.03 m)^2 = 9.0×10^-4 m^2. The oil film area A = 85×9.0×10^-4 = 7.65×10^-2 m^2. The volume of 50 drops of solution is 1 mL, so the volume of each drop of solution is 1/50 mL = 0.02 mL. The volume fraction of oleic acid in the solution is 0.6/1000, so the volume of pure oleic acid in each drop is 0.02×0.6/1000 mL = 1.2×10^-5 mL. Because 1 mL = 10^-6 m^3, V = 1.2×10^-11 m^3. method.method_draft: First inspect the image: it shows an irregular oleic-acid film boundary drawn on a uniform square grid. Count the number of grid squares covered by the film, treating nearly full squares as 1 and combining partial boundary squares into equivalent full squares. This gives about 85 small-square equivalents. From the text, each square has side length 30 mm = 0.03 m, so the film area is 85 × (0.03 m)^2 = 7.65 × 10^-2 m^2. Next use the text data: 50 drops increase volume by 1 mL, so one drop of solution is 1/50 mL = 0.02 mL. The solution contains 0.6 mL oleic acid per 1000 mL solution, so the oleic acid fraction is 0.6/1000. Thus pure oleic acid per drop is 0.02 × 0.6/1000 mL = 1.2 × 10^-5 mL = 1.2 × 10^-11 m^3. Since the film is monomolecular, estimate molecule diameter as film thickness d = V/A = (1.2 × 10^-11)/(7.65 × 10^-2) ≈ 1.57 × 10^-10 m.

When a drop of this solution is dripped into a shallow dish filled with water, the alcohol dissolves in the water, and the oleic acid spreads on the water surface, forming a stable monomolecular oil film as shown in the figure.

1. If the side length of each small square is $30\mathrm{mm}$, what is the area of the oleic acid film in square meters?
2. What is the volume of pure oleic acid in each drop of oleic acid alcohol solution in cubic meters?
3. Based on the above data, what is the estimated diameter of the oleic acid molecule in meters?

Using a dropper, 50 drops of the above solution are added to a measuring cylinder, increasing the volume of the solution in the cylinder by 1 mL. When a drop of this solution is dripped into a shallow dish filled with water, the alcohol dissolves in the water, and the oleic acid spreads on the water surface, forming a stable monomolecular oil film as shown in the figure. 1. If the side length of each small square is $30\mathrm{mm}$, what is the area of the oleic acid film in square meters? 2. What is the volume of pure oleic acid in each drop of oleic acid alcohol solution in cubic meters? 3. Based on the above data, what is the estimated diameter of the oleic acid molecule in meters?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, it is an irregular oleic acid film boundary drawn on uniform graph paper. Estimating according to the squares covered by the boundary in the figure, counting the small squares that are close to complete as 1, and combining and converting the incomplete small squares at the edge, the oil film occupies about 85 small squares.
Then reason and calculate: The side length of each small square is 30 mm = 0.03 m, so the area of each small square is (0.03 m)^2 = 9.0×10^-4 m^2. The oil film area A = 85×9.0×10^-4 = 7.65×10^-2 m^2.
The volume of 50 drops of solution is 1 mL, so the volume of each drop of solution is 1/50 mL = 0.02 mL. The volume fraction of oleic acid in the solution is 0.6/1000, so the volume of pure oleic acid in each drop is 0.02×0.6/1000 mL = 1.2×10^-5 mL. Because 1 mL = 10^-6 m^3, V = 1.2×10^-11 m^3.
When oleic acid forms a monomolecular film, the molecular diameter can be approximated as the film thickness d = V/A = (1.2×10^-11)/(7.65×10^-2) ≈ 1.57×10^-10 m.
